topics.label: Lecture Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture by introducing the lecturer and outlining the core learning objectives on cancer etiology and environmental carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Endogenous Factors, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by comparing intrinsic genetic errors and inherited predispositions with environmental exposures and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Viral Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how infectious agents and oncogenic viruses drive cancer development, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma and the lymphoma belt as a key model.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Chemical Carcinogenesis, Metabolic Activation, and Tumor Promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-infectious carcinogens cause DNA damage directly or via metabolic activation and distinguish between initiator mutagens and inflammatory tumor promoters.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to identify and evaluate carcinogenic agents.

topics.label: Lecture Summary and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This closing subtopic concludes the lecture by summarizing the key themes and reflecting on how individuals and society navigate carcinogen risks and benefits.
